name: Progressive Ray Casting for Volumetric Models on Mobile Devices
text:
# Progressive Ray Casting for Volumetric Models on Mobile Devices
## Overview
This method addresses the computational constraints of interactive volume rendering on mobile devices by combining multiresolution data structures with [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) techniques [S1, unofficial]. It solves the trade-off between frame rate and visual fidelity by using a lower-resolution dataset for exploration and progressively refining high-resolution details in regions of interest [S1, unofficial]. It incorporates Empty Space Skipping (ESS) and [Early Ray Termination (ERT)](#1002-empty-space-skipping.md) to reduce sampling overhead [S1, unofficial].
## Shared principles
The shared principles for this family are inherited from [Empty Space Skipping via Acceleration Structures](17387-empty-space-skipping-via-acceleration-structures.md) [G].
## Subtopics

The provided notes describe a system-level approach rather than distinct algorithmic subtopics [G]. The primary components are:

### Multiresolution Framework
Uses a lower-resolution dataset for interactive exploration and a high-resolution dataset for [progressive refinement](#14496-progressive-refinement.md) of regions of interest [S1, unofficial].

### Acceleration Integration
Incorporates ESS and ERT to reduce sampling overhead [S1, unofficial]. ESS starts ray sampling at the boundaries of a proxy geometry that roughly adjusts to non-transparent regions of the volume model, discarding transparent regions [S1, unofficial]. ERT finishes ray traversals whenever the computed color is considered opaque [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The method was proposed in a paper titled "Progressive Ray Casting for Volumetric Models on Mobile Devices" [S1, unofficial]. It addresses GPU horsepower limitations on mobile devices, noting that while models might fit in memory, frame rates can be inefficient for interactivity [S1, unofficial]. It builds upon acceleration techniques described by Krüger and Westermann [S1, unofficial]. It is designed for medical image inspection, where [orthographic projections](#4019-orthographic-projection.md) are the standard view [S1, unofficial].
## Sources
